    Cancellation and ray-path interlacement #

    Use BGRS cancellation to show that two equal nonzero ray paths with a common initial or final irreducible arrow are interlaced. This is the key injection behind the bound on the number of interlacement classes by local arrow valency in Roiter's theorem.

        theorem LargeIndecomposable.relatedPathInterlacementClass_card_le_of_code {Q : Type u} [Quiver Q] {R : PathContourRelation Q} (I : PathInterlacementRelation R) {i j : Q} (p : Quiver.Path i j) {A : Type w} [Finite A] (code : { q : Quiver.Path i j // R.related p q } → A) (hcode : ∀ (q r : { q : Quiver.Path i j // R.related p q }), code q = code r → I.interlaced ↑q ↑r) :
        Nat.card (RelatedPathInterlacementClass I p) ≤ Nat.card A

        If a code has the property that equal codes force two representatives to be interlaced, the number of interlacement classes is bounded by the number of codes. Choosing the first arrow as the code gives Roiter's local valency bound once common-first-arrow interlacement is available.
